analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The source text introduces three key concepts — מחשבה (thought), חכמה (wisdom/chokhmah), and אמת (truth) — none of which appear in bechina-typed edges for this Torah. The text distinguishes them definitionally and causally: thought (מחשבה) is what rises in the mind spontaneously; chokhmah (חכמה) is what actively builds structures in the intellect and is more precious; truth (אמת) is the essential quality that must accompany both, without which they produce their opposite. The relationship between מחשבה and חכמה is a contrast/distinction (chokhmah is higher than thought), not a bechina equivalence — the Rebbe is differentiating them, not equating them. The relationship between thought/chokhmah and אמת is conditional/causal (they must be in truth, or they produce the opposite). No bechina equating language ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', 'כנ"ל') appears anywhere in the source text. Therefore no additions to packages can be proposed — there are no packages to add to.
